replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, you get two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, two complex roots. Finally, use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). I focus on simplicity and avoiding jargon to make it relatable.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f’(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. Check if they’re maxima or minima using the second derivative test: if f''(x) > 0, it’s a minimum; if f''(x) < 0, it’s a maximum. I keep explanations visual and hands-on to match my practical learning style.
